# sonnet-2-again — depth 7, and the first deliberate descent

> **Reconstructed, not written by the player.** This run finished without writing a report: it reported to the session that started it, and that account lived in a conversation rather than in the repository. What follows was written afterwards from the run's own record, decisions and notebook, plus the player's handback where there was one. The player's own words are only in `notebook.md`.

291 asks, 1,107 keypresses, turn 10,416. Half-Troll Warrior, **depth 7 (350
feet), character level 8**, wealth 2,025, alive when the budget ran out.
Carried on from `sonnet-2` at ask 152, turn 6,026, depth 6.

## What it settled

Four runs and some 350 asks had never found a down staircase in the dungeon.
This one did, and it used the game's own pathfinding to do it:

    ask 228  depth 6  turn 9117  l>   the cursor jumps to the known staircase
    ask 229  depth 6  turn 9117  g    walks the path: 11 steps, 110 game turns
    ask 230  depth 6  turn 9227  >    status line "Down staircase" -> depth 7
    ask 231  depth 7  turn 9227  <    LF:6 on arrival, leave and reroll
    ask 232  depth 6  turn 9227  >    down again for a fresh DL7

`lxg` is a free autoexplore hop; `l>g` walks to a known down staircase; `l<g`
walks back up. Each must go alone in its ask: a key sent after `g` interrupts
the walk after one step, so `lxglxglxg` gives three one-square hops rather
than three walks - measured both ways at asks 156-164.

## What else it found

- **A reroll costs two asks.** Stairs are connected, so `<` then `>` gives a
  fresh level of the same depth, and a key sent after a level change is
  swallowed, so each needs a trailing space.
- **Reroll on a level feeling of 5 or more.** The first DL7 showed LF:6 and
  was left; the third was "tame, sheltered" and was kept.
- **`[` lists the visible monsters** with asleep or awake, where `l` only ever
  returned the player's own square.
- **The DL6 staircase was the dead end it had already stood on.** "There is a
  wall in the way!" had hidden the terrain line, so the `>` was only seen once
  `lxg` moved away and the map drew it. Read the terrain after every dead end.
- **Large kobolds** are 65 hit points and take 4-5 rounds at 16 damage a round
  with a cutlass; Fang died in two rounds at character level 7.
- **Aiming an unknown wand at a sleeping tamer was Haste Monster.** It woke
  hasted, slowed and confused the character, and cost about 15 asks and 50 hit
  points. Do not test an unknown wand on something you mean to fight.

## Where it was left

Slowed, recently confused, in a doorway of a lit room with a yellow jelly in
it, one Cure Light Wounds, two Phase Door, one Word of Recall - and a hasted
tamer that fled at about 30% health and is still alive somewhere.
